profile.reading: VaultLogix is a Scottsdale, Arizona based provider of offsite data backup, disaster recovery, and business continuity services, and business directories place VaultLogix LLC in the same Scottsdale, AZ 85260 postal area as this location. The VaultLogix brand has since been folded into CyberFortress, a managed backup as a service and disaster recovery as a service company that offers cloud backed data protection built on partner infrastructure such as Veeam Data Cloud and Wasabi cloud storage, and that still operates a legacy VaultLogix customer portal for existing clients. Companies in this line of business typically sell managed backup software and coordinate storage of client data across third party cloud and colocation infrastructure rather than owning and operating their own purpose built data center buildings, and nothing found in company or public records indicates VaultLogix ever operated a dedicated data center at this Scottsdale address. It is best understood as a sales, support, and account management office for a data protection service provider, not as a data center facility, so no capacity, square footage, or other facility specification is published here.
profile.research_note: VaultLogix LLC confirmed as a real backup/DRaaS brand located in Scottsdale AZ 85260 (matches this node's postal area) via business directory listings, now folded into CyberFortress (cyberfortress.com still runs a legacy 'VaultLogix Advantage Partners' portal at portal.vaultlogix.com). Nominatim reverse geocode at the exact stored coordinates returns an unrelated interior-design shop as the nearest indexed feature, meaning the exact building occupant could not be pinned to street level, but the postal area and business type are confirmed. This reads as a managed-service sales/support office, not a facility housing dedicated server infrastructure, so specs_unpublished is set.

reading.body:
VaultLogix operates a sales and support office for a managed backup service, not a data center, so it contributes zero megawatts to Arizona's compute infrastructure.

The company coordinates storage across third-party cloud and colocation providers rather than owning dedicated facilities. Business records confirm the Scottsdale location as an account management office for CyberFortress, which resells backup and disaster recovery services built on partner infrastructure like Veeam and Wasabi. This is a service layer, not a building with power draw.

Arizona publishes power capacity for only 4 of its 56 mapped data centers, totaling 512 megawatts. VaultLogix's address would not add to that total even if it were operational infrastructure. When assessing the state's ability to support AI workloads, this site should be excluded from capacity models.
